item.title: Absence of $\sigma$-criticality in Short-Range Spin Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2611.31584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of $\sigma$-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that $\sigma$-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called $\sigma$-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of $\sigma$-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of $\sigma$-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.
item.dc:creator: C. M. Newman, D. L. Stein

item.title: Conformality lost in Anderson localization in infinite dimensions, and regained in finite dimensions: a phenomenological theory of the Anderson transition in high dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the recent works on Anderson localization when the number of spatial dimensions $d\to\infty$ can be framed into the scenario dubbed it conformality lost [Kaplan et al., Phys. Rev. D 80, 125005 (2009)], which occurs when two fixed points of the RG collide and become complex. This framing makes it natural for a two-parameter scaling flow \`a la Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) to control all the observables of the theory as conjectured in [Vanoni et al., PNAS 121, e2401955121 (2024)]. We also use this as a starting point for an $\epsilon$ expansion of the RG equations in $\epsilon=1/d\ll 1$, and find phenomenological RG equations which fit the numerical results in dimensions $d\gtrsim 4$.
item.dc:creator: Antonello Scardicchio, Carlo Vanoni

item.title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.31384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The celebrated Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborne, Rhine Samajdar, Andrew A. Houck

item.title: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps
item.description: arXiv:2611.32236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finding the ground states of quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge in physics and quantum chemistry. Imaginary-time evolution (ITE) offers a natural, widely used route, but its convergence is typically asymptotic. Variational approaches restrict this evolution to parameterized manifolds, with neural quantum states (NQS) providing flexible representations commonly optimized via stochastic reconfiguration (SR). Their performance depends on the geometry of the variational manifold, the convergence properties of ITE, and the stability of finite-step explicit (forward) integrators. By exploiting local geometric information of the energy landscape, the recently introduced augmented imaginary-time evolution (AITE) can, in principle, reach the ground state in finite imaginary time. To exploit the accelerated convergence of AITE in NQS optimization, we first combine an implicit Euler step with Galerkin projection to derive an implicit SR scheme that permits large, stable steps and substantially outperforms conventional methods. We use it to formulate an implicit version of AITE and show that its acceleration persists under variational projection and finite-step integration with asymptotically quadratic convergence of the energy error. With finite sampling, implicit schemes yield consistent gains, and implicit AITE becomes increasingly advantageous.
item.dc:creator: Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Thomas D. K\"uhne, Fedor \v{S}imkovic IV, Prachi Sharma, Carlos L. Benavides-Riveros, Werner Dobrautz

item.title: Parametric neural-network wavefunctions across a bosonic phase transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.33150v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose Boseformer, a universal attention-based neural-network architecture for representing the wavefunctions of particles with bosonic quantum statistics, including superfluid and crystal phases. The model is trained to generate the wavefunction as a function of a Hamiltonian parameter across the quantum phase transition between these phases. Once trained with variational Monte Carlo optimization, it can serve as a foundation model describing the phase transition without the need to retrain it for individual parameter values. We demonstrate our method on a system of two-dimensional bosons with $1/r^3$ repulsive interaction.
item.dc:creator: Daniil S. Antonenko, Liang Fu, Leonid I. Glazman

item.title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.33155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].
item.dc:creator: Aiden Mains, Danile Salib, Christopher Leong, Bitan Roy

item.title: Frustrated neurons: Energy landscapes and relaxation dynamics in repulsive phase oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2606.02512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Geometrical frustration, a central paradigm in condensed matter physics, provides a unifying language for systems in which locally preferred interactions cannot be made globally compatible. Here, we use this language to formulate a minimal theory of frustrated neural timing, mapping repulsively coupled rhythmic units onto antiferromagnetic $XY$ models. In this formulation, the condensed-matter concepts of local constraints, degenerate ground-state manifolds, metastability, and quench dynamics are used to guide our analysis of structured neural phase dynamics. This paper analyzes a hierarchy of geometries, beginning with a triangle as the minimal frustrated motif with two chiral 120{\deg} timing states, then a tetrahedron whose reduced ground-state manifold consists of intersecting continuous branches associated with antipodal pairings, and finally a kagome lattice on which local constraints define a constrained three-coloring manifold. The kagome lattice reveals that zero-temperature relaxation suppresses global synchrony but typically selects low-energy metastable torque-balanced states rather than exact ground states. We then show how the phase theory can be carried back towards biophysical neural models by treating the minimal framework as an effective-interaction target, where geometrical timing frustration arises from preferred phase lags that become incompatible around closed motifs. Our results suggest that weak global coherence in neural systems doesn't necessarily signal disordered activity, but can instead reflect structured local timing order within a frustrated dynamical landscape.
item.dc:creator: Brandon B. Le

item.title: Inner sublattice competition: a minimal mechanism for reentrant localizations in Aubry-Andr\'e lattice
item.description: arXiv:2606.24720v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a double mosaic Aubry-Andr\'e (DMAA) model with two independent quasiperiodic potentials assigned to corresponding even and odd sublattices of the AA lattice, and show that the competition between them gives rise to multiple localization-delocalization transitions under single-parameter tuning. Such reentrant localizations are verified by comprehensive numerical characterizations including the inverse participation ratio, normalized participation ratio, fractal dimension, and real-space wavefunction distributions. Simulations based on a continuous polariton model yield consistent results, confirming the experimental feasibility of the predicted phenomena. This inner sublattice competition mechanism works in a minimal way for reentrant localizations without additional ingredients or dynamical modifications such as long-range hopping, mixed quasiperiodic and random disorder, or non-Hermitian gain and loss, offering a concise route to engineer reentrant localization based on the canonical AA lattice family.
item.dc:creator: Hangdong Qiu, Yunhua Wang

item.title: Atom as an Agent: Emergent Order by Collective Predictive Coding
item.description: arXiv:2610.36673v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: What is the intrinsic reason of emergence of macroscopic order parameter out of microscopic systems? In this article, we apply to physics the collective predictive coding (CPC), the theory of language/symbol emergence. As our language emerges out of our human communications, physical macroscopic order parameter emerges out of communications among atoms --- each atom is regarded as an agent who predicts each other's behavior through inference. We present three examples of classical spin systems: two-dimensional ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, a two-dimensional spin model with competing stripe orders, and the fully connected Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model. In all of these examples, proper macroscopic order parameters including the replica overlap emerge automatically through communication informatics of CPC, only from observed spin configurations. We call the learned macroscopic coordinate the collective predictive order. Furthermore, for the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, the equilibrium distribution of the collective predictive order yields an emergent potential with the symmetry and thermal evolution characteristic of a Landau potential. Notably, the emergence of the collective predictive order does not refer to any structure of microscopic Hamiltonians/Lagrangians. Thus our ``Atom-as-an-Agent" (AaaA) principle offers a completely data-driven method for the emergence of macroscopic order, that is, machine learning physics.
item.dc:creator: Koji Hashimoto, Tadahiro Taniguchi

item.title: Quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.38943v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization. Quantum dynamics based on quantum annealing (QA) or the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is used to engineer the transition kernel. Increasing the annealing time in QA or the number of layers in QAOA enables transitions to explore distant configurations while suppressing large energy changes. The Hamming-space delocalization originates from operator spreading, whereas the energy-space localization arises from a dynamically generated correlation. For optimization, we propose quantum-echo local optimization. For the ferromagnetic Ising chain, increasing the annealing time or circuit depth yields a nearly quadratic improvement in the dependence of the mean first-passage time on the inverse optimality gap compared with random single-spin flips. For the random Ising model, increasing these parameters initially improves optimization performance, whereas further increases degrade performance in QA and lead to saturation in QAOA. Quantum-echo greedy descent substantially improves the performance, highlighting the complementary roles of quantum dynamics in exploration and greedy descent in exploitation. These results establish quantum-echo dynamics as a framework for engineering structured transition kernels and provide a route to using finite-resource quantum many-body dynamics as a computational primitive for iterative optimization.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuhiko Shirai
